# v2: add evaluation.

<div class="flow" style="margin-bottom: 1.5em;">
  <div class="flow-box">Generate</div>
  <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="flow-box">Evaluate</div>

Score each quote on quality dimensions. Keep the top-ranked.

The evaluator rewarded vivid, specific writing. But vivid writing without a payoff ranked just as highly as vivid writing with one.

Generate variations of top quotes, then re-evaluate.

> The caramelized chili oil **explained** why microwaved nachos can never taste like home.
> The caramelized chili oil **was the reason** microwaved nachos could never taste like home.

<p class="note">A mutation. Both scored highly. The concept was already weak; the mutation changed three words.</p>

Each run still started from scratch.

# MAP-Elites: one champion per niche.

From quality-diversity research ([Mouret & Clune, 2015](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1504.04909)).<br/>
6 rhetorical devices x 5 tones = **30 cells**. Each holds one champion.

| | funny | inspirational | self-deprecating | deadpan | philosophical |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| irony | | | | | |
| understatement | | | | | |
| wordplay | | | | | |
| paradox | | | | | |
| observation | | | | | |
| absurdism | | | | | |

The grid provides the variety.

<!-- You don't ask for variety. You build it into what the archive can hold. A quote using irony to be funny occupies a different cell from one using understatement to be philosophical. -->

---

# The pipeline: run 1.

<div class="flow">
  <div class="flow-box">Generate</div>
  <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="flow-box">Classify</div>
  <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="flow-box">Evaluate</div>
  <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="flow-box">Archive</div>
</div>

- **Generate**: ask the model for fresh quotes
- **Classify**: which cell? (rhetorical device × emotional tone)
- **Evaluate**: score on twist, coherence, freshness, economy
- **Archive**: empty to start; any quote above the minimum score enters its cell

---

# From run 2: the loop.

<div class="flow">
  <div class="flow-box">Archive</div>
  <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="flow-box">Generate<br>+ Mutate</div>
  <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="flow-box">Classify</div>
  <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="flow-box">Evaluate</div>
  <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="flow-box">Archive</div>
</div>

Archive champions become mutation parents. Each mutation also receives the **evaluator's per-item critique** for that parent, so it targets the specific flaws rather than varying at random.

Fresh generation is guided toward empty and weak cells. A quote enters only if it scores higher than the current champion. Then the cycle repeats.

<!-- Displacement example from office-5: "My morning coffee isn't fuel for ambition, it's a liquid bribe to accept I won't wake up." (0.73) was displaced by a mutation that removed one word — "My coffee isn't fuel for ambition..." (0.86). Same cell, one word changed, clear score gain. -->
<!-- Both the generation and mutation prompts have a built-in draft chain: the model writes a draft, critiques it, and revises before producing its final output. This is a chain-of-thought pattern encoded in the JSON schema field ordering. -->


---

# The evaluator scores and rejects.

Every item, every run. Not a human: the model itself.

> "The cursor pauses, calculating if the code is good enough to let you breathe."

<div style="font-size: 1.55rem; margin-top: 0.6em; line-height: 1.7;">
<strong>coherence: 0.30</strong> &nbsp;(min 0.60 required) &nbsp;"Cursors are passive indicators; the causal logic does not hold."<br>
<strong>freshness: 0.40</strong> &nbsp;(min 0.50 required) &nbsp;"Uses the common 'AI has feelings' trope without a fresh twist."
</div>

<p class="note">Does not enter the archive. Most generated items do not.</p>

<!-- Human review happens separately and infrequently: the user looks at the current archive champions and accepts or rejects them. -->

---

# How the loop learns.

**Automatically, every 5 runs:** the evaluator's per-item critiques from recent rejected items are distilled into craft principles and injected into generation and mutation prompts. Example output:

> "The quote must establish a causal link that is physically or logically grounded rather than forcing a connection between unrelated concepts."

**Occasionally, by hand:** the current archive champions are reviewed. Each can be accepted or rejected with a reason. Those reasons feed a separate distillation into the evaluation prompt. Accepted quotes become positive examples for the evaluator; the cell stays open for something better.

<!-- _class: dark -->

# A system that gets better over time.

- **Quality**: each cell holds the best-scoring quote found so far
- **Variety**: the grid structure provides it
- **Generation improves automatically**: craft principles from the evaluator's own critiques
- **Evaluation improves with input**: occasional human review refines the quality criteria
